article-1.title: FundGate guideline for investment managers
article-1.description: A complete guide to the platform for investment managers of venture funds
article-1.content:
# FundGate investment manager guideline

This guide explains how a fund's investment manager works with incoming applications in FundGate — from the first application through the deal and on to portfolio support. The founder-facing "how to apply" instructions live in a separate article.

## The "Startups" board
Every application lands on a kanban board. Columns are the funnel stages:
- New applications — just received, not reviewed yet
- Under review — initial screening and collection of materials
- Pipeline — projects in active work and deal preparation
- Portfolio — companies the fund has invested in

A card can be dragged between columns — status and stage change automatically. Each column has a checklist of steps (KYC, Data Room, screening, and so on). The fund director configures columns and steps to match the fund's process through the column builder.

## Working with an application
Opening a startup card, the manager sees:
- the AI assessment — automatic scoring and a short summary of product, market, team and financials; use it as a first filter, not as the final decision
- the company profile, financial indicators and uploaded documents (pitch deck, reports)
- assignment of the manager responsible for the project
- the interaction log and comments — record calls, meetings and notes
- a chat with the founder right from the card

## Moving through the funnel
Move the project along the stages as its steps are completed. On each transition:
- the system checks unfinished checklist steps and warns you
- the founder receives a status-change notification, including in their personal cabinet
- moving to "Portfolio" opens the deal parameters: amount, valuation, investment type

## Investment committee
When a project is ready for a decision, it goes to the IC. The process runs through stages, and the current owner of the next step is visible on the "Investment committee" screen:
- Shortlist — the manager builds the agenda, uploads the document, the CEO or a deputy approves it
- Voting — IC members vote "for" or "against" each project
- Legal opinion, then approval by the deputy and the director
- Protocol signatures — participants sign the final protocol

## Portfolio
After the deal the company enters the portfolio. The manager maintains:
- metrics: MOIC, runway, MRR, growth rate, burn
- health status (green / yellow / red) — automatically by thresholds or manually
- quarterly reports and AI digests
- the cap table and round history

## Roles and access
- Director (CEO) — full access, board configuration, final decisions
- Deputies — approvals at their own stages
- Investment managers — running their own projects
- Investment committee member — voting and signing protocols; the portfolio is available in view mode
- Lawyer, financier, technical specialist — their specialised stages

## Notifications and updates
Keep an eye on the "Notifications" section (events on your projects) and "Updates" (platform news and guides).

article-founder-submit.title: How a founder submits an application to FundGate
article-founder-submit.description: A step-by-step guide for startups: how to apply for investment through the FundGate platform
article-founder-submit.content:
# How to submit an application to FundGate

The application is submitted through the embedded FundGate form (widget) on the fund's website — you do not need to create a separate password-protected account on the platform.

## Step 1: Sign in with an email code
Open the FundGate form on the fund's website. To sign in, enter your email and confirm it with a one-time code (OTP) — no password needed. The same email later gives you access to the personal cabinet with your application.

## Step 2: Upload the pitch deck (autofill)
Start by uploading your pitch deck (PDF or PPT). FundGate AI parses the presentation and fills the form in for you. After that, go through every step and check each field — the AI can make mistakes or leave something blank. The form can also be filled in manually.

## Step 3: Company profile
Check and correct if needed:
- Startup name
- Industry
- Short description
- Team size
- Year founded

## Step 4: Financial indicators
Provide your financial metrics:
- Current revenue
- Revenue growth
- Amount requested from the fund
- Total round size
- Previous rounds (if any)

## Step 5: Documents
- Pitch deck — required (PDF / PPT)
- Logo — optional
- One-pager — optional (PDF / DOCX)
- Financial model — optional (XLS / XLSX / CSV)

## Step 6: Submission
Submit the application. The AI system runs an initial analysis, after which the application reaches the fund's managers.

## After submission
In the personal cabinet (sign-in by email code) you have:
- Status — the current review stage
- History — the event feed for your application
- Chat — correspondence with the fund's investment manager

Review usually takes 5-7 business days.

article-2.title: How FundGate AI analytics works
article-2.description: Find out how SmartVal values your startup
article-2.content:
# How FundGate AI analytics works

## SmartVal Engine
SmartVal is our AI-powered startup valuation system, built on several methodologies:

### 1. Berkus Method
Early-stage valuation based on qualitative factors:
- Team quality
- Product prototype
- Strategic relationships
- Sales and marketing

### 2. Scorecard Method
Comparative analysis against other startups in your industry and region.

### 3. DCF Analysis
Discounted cash flow for startups with revenue.

## FundGate Score (0-100)
A composite score that takes into account:
- [team] **Team** (25%) - experience, expertise, complementarity
- [product] **Product** (25%) - innovation, product-market fit
- [market] **Market** (20%) - size, growth, competition
- [finance] **Finance** (20%) - metrics, unit economics, profitability
- [traction] **Traction** (10%) - growth, customers, engagement

## Analysis results
Once processing is finished you receive:
- An estimated valuation
- The FundGate Score
- A detailed analysis of strengths and weaknesses
- A recommendation for investors

# Integration with StartupBase

## What is StartupBase?
StartupBase is the largest startup platform in Uzbekistan, bringing together entrepreneurs, investors and experts.

## How does the integration work?
If you are already registered on StartupBase, you can:
1. Sign in with a single account (SSO)
2. Import your startup data automatically
3. Submit an application in one click

## Benefits
- Fast application submission
- Data synchronisation
- Real-time updates
- Access to the startup network

## How to connect it?
Go to your account settings and click "Connect StartupBase". Follow the instructions to authorise the connection.

article-4.title: Startup selection criteria
article-4.content:
# Startup selection criteria

## Key factors
When reviewing applications, fund managers assess:

### 1. Team
- Industry experience
- Previous successes
- Complementary skills
- Ability to execute

### 2. Product
- Uniqueness of the solution
- Product-market fit
- Technological advantage
- Defensibility (patents, know-how)

### 3. Market
- TAM/SAM/SOM size
- Market growth rate
- Competitive environment
- Barriers to entry

### 4. Business model
- Monetisation
- Unit economics
- Scalability
- LTV/CAC

### 5. Traction
- User/revenue growth
- Retention rate
- Virality
- Customer testimonials

## What improves your chances?
- A strong team with a track record
- Proven traction
- A large, fast-growing market
- Healthy unit economics
- Protected technology

settings.title: System settings
settings.totalScoreNote: Σ(Score ÷ 4 × weight). Strong ≥ 80%; Healthy ≥ 50%; Need attention ≥ 35%; At Risk ≥ 15%; Critical < 15%. Score 5 remains a bonus above 100%.
settings.hint: Fund settings and auxiliary metric thresholds. The final automatic status is driven only by Total Score from the specification.
settings.usdToUzsNote: Used for dual currency and total values in UZS. Update monthly.
settings.usdToKztNote: Used for Kazakhstan portfolio companies and the future multi-currency mode.
settings.segmentMarginThresholdsHelp: Values are percentages. Green starts at the configured value, yellow starts at the lower threshold, and anything below yellow is red. The segment can be selected in the table; until then it is inferred from industry and business model.
settings.runwayGreenNote: ≥ {{value}} months is considered a sustainable cash buffer.
settings.runwayYellowNote: ≥ {{value}} months = needs attention; below that = red capital risk.
settings.momGreenNote: ≥ {{value}}% monthly growth is considered good momentum.
settings.momYellowNote: ≥ 0% = growth exists but is weak; below 0% = red signal.
settings.moicGreenNote: ≥ {{value}}x means the portfolio company looks healthy by multiple.
settings.churnYellowNote: ≤ {{value}}% = needs attention; above that = red retention risk.
settings.fundNameNote: Displayed in headers, reports, and portfolio views.
settings.reportingPeriodNote: Current quarter for quarterly reports and the traction tracker.
settings.baseCurrencyNote: Primary calculation currency: investment, valuation, MOIC, and value bridge.
settings.followOnCriterionNote: MOIC ≥ {{moic}}x plus runway ≥ {{runway}} mo. and non-negative MoM growth.
settings.followOnRunwayNote: Minimum runway for follow-on watchlist candidates.
settings.reminderAudienceNote: Only startups in the portfolio (`status=portfolio`). Pipeline, review, rejected, and archive do not receive requests.
settings.reminderPeriodNote: The backend chooses the previous quarter, sets a due date in 14 days, and avoids duplicates if a request/report already exists for the period.
settings.reminderChannelNote: Email is sent through the current notification service. SMS is sent through Twilio only when SMS env vars are configured; dev without override does not send real SMS.

platformReport.subtitle: A verified snapshot of the production database: the six partner funds listed on fundgate.uz, their application flow, and how application quality is trending.

sections.scaleHint: A single startup submission can go to several funds at once, so “unique startups” and “cards in fund CRMs” are different figures: the first shows the applicant flow, the second the workload the platform took off the funds. Startups are merged with the same algorithm as the public counter on fundgate.uz.
sections.qualityHint: Average FundGate score on a 100-point scale. Calculated only on unique submissions with a completed analysis — copies of one application across funds are excluded.
sections.monthlyTableHint: The same figures in table form — for the record and for cross-checking.
sections.fundsHint: “Cards” is how many applications the fund received; “unique” is how many distinct startups are behind them.

stats.managers: Employees of these funds work in the CRM
stats.speed: Median AI scoring time per application
stats.portfolio: Startups already taken into a portfolio
stats.fundsPerStartup: Funds receive one submission on average

charts.monthlyHint: Bars show the average application score, the line shows the share of applications scoring 60+, i.e. those a fund will seriously consider.
charts.componentsHint: The six FundGate scoring blocks, normalised to a percentage of each block’s maximum. Most of the gain comes from the pitch deck and the product description.
charts.channelHint: Control check: direct applications through fund forms (iframe) only. The scoring version stayed at 1.0.0 for the whole period, so the growth cannot be explained by an algorithm or channel change.
charts.completenessHint: Average number of filled-in form fields. Pitch-deck autofill and in-form hints raised application completeness — hence the higher scores.
charts.geographyHint: Share of submissions that state a country.
charts.industriesHint: Top 10 industries by number of submissions.
charts.funnelHint: All “startup → fund” cards across the six funds. One startup can sit in several funds’ pipelines at once.
charts.toolingHint: How many times the key features were used. These counters are platform-wide, not limited to the six funds.

tooling.autofillJobs: Pitch decks parsed by AI autofill
tooling.aiChats: Conversations with the fund AI assistant

method.source: Cards of the six partner funds listed on fundgate.uz were selected. There are no test or QA records among them.
method.dedup: Startups are merged with the same algorithm as the public counter on fundgate.uz: by the shared application identifier and by the “name + phone + website” triple. The calculation is reconciled with the live endpoint — across the whole platform it returns the same 540 unique startups, and 416 for the six funds. Quality metrics are additionally split by submission date so copies of one application are not counted twice.
method.score: The final FundGate score on a 100-point scale: application completeness 20, pitch deck 20, traction 20, team 15, product 15, materials 10. Only applications with a successfully completed analysis and a non-zero score are counted.
method.speed: Median time from submission to a finished AI score
